title: US embargo on Cuba from 1960
summary: On 19 October 1960 the United States put general export controls on Cuba, prohibiting nearly all American exports except certain foods and medicines, after Cuban seizures of US-owned property. President Kennedy extended this to a full trade embargo effective 7 February 1962, and the embargo remains in force in later decades.

uncertainty.note: The State Department chronology dates the embargo to 19 October 1960; the National Security Archive dates the State Department announcement to 20 October. The end date marks only the full trade embargo of 1962; the embargo continued after it.

as_recorded.value: Oct 19, 1960: U.S. imposes economic embargo on Cuba, except food and medicine
Oct. 20, 1960: the State Department announced general controls to prohibit American exports to Cuba

where.modern_name: Washington, DC, United States (where the controls were issued; effect on Cuba)

importance.justification: The start of the longest-running US sanctions regime, shaping US-Cuba relations and Cuba's economy for decades.

related.because: Cuban government seizures of US property after the revolution led the US to impose export controls.

beats.caption: The US imposed general export controls on Cuba, prohibiting nearly all exports except food, medicines and medical supplies.
The controls followed Cuba's nationalization of US-owned businesses and US cuts to Cuban sugar purchases.
President Kennedy proclaimed a full embargo on all trade with Cuba, effective 7 February 1962.
